default.title: MOVE OUT?
default.speaker: Office friend
default.text: 'Share a flat near office? ₹8,000 rent each.' Living at home: ₹3,000 to family and a long bus ride.

pocket_money.title: MOVE OUT?
pocket_money.speaker: Colleague
pocket_money.intro: First job in Gachibowli: ₹20,000 a month.
pocket_money.text: A colleague offers a room nearby for ₹8,000. Home is a 90-minute bus ride; Mom asks ₹3,000 a month.

scholarship.title: MOVE OUT?
scholarship.speaker: Old classmates
scholarship.text: Friends from college want a flat together: ₹8,000 each. At home, you'd give ₹3,000 and commute.

earner.title: MOVE OUT?
earner.speaker: Co-worker
earner.text: A flat near work is ₹8,000. Home needs your ₹3,000 and a long ride every day.

choices.lesson: ₹8,000 of ₹20,000 on rent leaves little for saving or shocks. Rent should fit the month, not eat it.
choices.hint: What's left after rent, food and travel?

choices.lesson: The ride costs time, but ₹5,000 a month builds your buffer fast. Move when rent fits, not before.
Comparing found a cheaper room. Rent at a fifth of your salary still leaves room to save.

default.title: NO-COST EMI
default.speaker: Phone shop
default.text: 'New ₹24,000 phone on no-cost EMI! Only ₹2,000 a month.' Fine print: ₹999 processing fee. Your phone works fine.

pocket_money.title: NO-COST EMI
pocket_money.speaker: Phone shop
pocket_money.text: Everyone at office has the new phone. Shop: '₹2,000 a month, no-cost EMI!' Fine print: ₹999 fee.

scholarship.title: NO-COST EMI
scholarship.speaker: Cousin
scholarship.text: Your cousin: 'EMI phones pay for themselves!' Shop: '₹2,000 a month, no-cost!' Fine print: ₹999 fee.

earner.title: NO-COST EMI
earner.speaker: Phone shop
earner.text: Your old phone is scratched but works. Shop: 'New one for ₹2,000 a month, no-cost EMI!' Fine print: ₹999 fee.

choices.lesson: 'No-cost' still cost ₹999, and ₹2,000 leaves every month for a year. An EMI is a loan, and it follows you.
choices.hint: If it's 'no-cost', what is the ₹999 for?

choices.lesson: Six months of saving buys it outright: no fee, no EMI, no monthly hook.
Needs, not wants: your phone works. The best EMI is the one you never needed.

default.title: SAFETY NET
default.speaker: Aunty
default.text: Salary: ₹20,000. Aunty asks: 'If your job stopped tomorrow, how many months could you manage?'

pocket_money.title: SAFETY NET
pocket_money.speaker: Mom
pocket_money.text: Mom asks: 'If your job stops, can you manage?' You have no savings yet. Salary: ₹20,000.

scholarship.title: SAFETY NET
scholarship.speaker: Aunty
scholarship.text: You remember waiting months for the allowance. Now salary comes monthly. How big a cushion do you need?

earner.title: SAFETY NET
earner.speaker: Aunty
earner.text: You remember weeks when shop pay just stopped. Now there's a salary. Time to build a real cushion?

choices.lesson: Aim for 3–6 months of expenses, built bit by bit, automatically. That's an emergency buffer.

choices.text: I'LL SAVE WHEN I NEED TO
choices.lesson: Emergencies don't give notice. By the time you 'need to', it's too late to save.
choices.hint: Do emergencies send a warning first?

choices.text: A CREDIT CARD IS MY BUFFER
choices.lesson: A card isn't a buffer; it's a loan with high interest. Savings are a buffer.
choices.hint: What does a card charge if you can't repay in full?

choices.lesson: A start! But one month is thin. Keep going until you have 3–6 months.

default.title: FAMILY LOAN
default.speaker: Uncle
default.text: 'Lend me ₹10,000 for my shop, beta. Three months, I'll return it.' That's half your salary and most of your savings.

pocket_money.title: FAMILY LOAN
pocket_money.speaker: Uncle
pocket_money.text: The uncle who gave you Sankranti money: 'Lend me ₹10,000 for three months?' It's most of your savings.

scholarship.title: FAMILY LOAN
scholarship.speaker: Relative
scholarship.text: The relative who helped with your ePASS papers asks for ₹10,000 'for three months'. It's most of your savings.

earner.title: FAMILY LOAN
earner.speaker: Old shop owner
earner.text: The man who gave you your first job asks to borrow ₹10,000 for three months. It's most of your savings.

choices.lesson: Your buffer is now someone else's promise. Lend only what you could afford never to see again.
choices.hint: What if your own emergency comes before the money returns?

choices.lesson: Help with what you can afford to lose, and call it a gift. Your savings, and the relationship, stay safe.
A smaller amount, written down with a date, is fair to both of you. Still, lend only what you can wait for.

default.title: START EARLY?
default.speaker: Bank clerk
default.intro: Banyan Savings is made up. Assumes 8% a year; real returns vary.
default.text: 'Put ₹2,000 a month in Banyan Savings. Starting at 23 instead of 33 makes a huge difference.'

pocket_money.title: START EARLY?
pocket_money.speaker: Bank clerk
pocket_money.intro: Banyan Savings is made up. Assumes 8% a year; real returns vary.
pocket_money.text: You open your first own account. The clerk: '₹2,000 a month in Banyan Savings, starting now?'

scholarship.title: START EARLY?
scholarship.speaker: Bank clerk
scholarship.intro: Banyan Savings is made up. Assumes 8% a year; real returns vary.
scholarship.text: The same branch where your allowance landed: 'Your salary's here now. ₹2,000 a month into Banyan?'

earner.title: START EARLY?
earner.speaker: Bank clerk
earner.intro: Banyan Savings is made up. Assumes 8% a year; real returns vary.
earner.text: For years every rupee went out as soon as it came. The clerk: 'Start ₹2,000 a month in Banyan?'

choices.lesson: Starting 10 years earlier roughly doubles the result: growth on growth needs time. That's compounding.
Waiting 10 years loses more than 10 years of saving; it loses the growth on that growth.
choices.hint: Which grows more: 35 years of growth, or 25?

choices.text: SAVE IT IN A CASH BOX
choices.lesson: Saving is great! But a cash box never grows, and inflation shrinks it. Let savings compound.

default.title: DOUBLE MONEY
default.speaker: Chat group
default.text: Screenshots everywhere: 'Invest ₹10,000, get ₹20,000 in 6 months! Guaranteed! Only 3 slots left!'

pocket_money.title: DOUBLE MONEY
pocket_money.speaker: Cousin
pocket_money.text: Your cousin adds you to an 'investment club': '₹10,000 becomes ₹20,000 in 6 months, guaranteed!'

scholarship.title: DOUBLE MONEY
scholarship.speaker: Old classmate
scholarship.text: An old classmate: 'I doubled my money in 6 months! Join with ₹10,000, only 3 slots left!'

earner.title: DOUBLE MONEY
earner.speaker: Regular customer
earner.text: A regular customer: 'My scheme doubles ₹10,000 in 6 months. Guaranteed. Only for people I trust.'

choices.lesson: Guaranteed + double + hurry = scam. Nothing honest promises to double your money in 6 months.
choices.hint: Can anything real be guaranteed AND double in 6 months?

choices.lesson: Fake apps show fake profits so you send more. If you can't withdraw it, it was never real.

effects.label: No answer. You left the group.

choices.lesson: Real investments are registered and never 'guarantee' doubling. No straight answer means walk away.
Safe. Next time warn the others too; these groups target whole families.
